note: Sixteenths counted "1 e & a" in the rhythm game at "level": "intermediate" (the beat:4 ladder), then a rest on the number and a rest on the "&" against the metronome, then both swapped over drums. The old Stage choice of tempos is moves (50 to 70), the drums section keeps its distance above it, and every section has one feel to reach or one thing to do when it goes wrong.

exercise.title: Sixteenths and rests
exercise.why: A sixteenth is a quarter of a beat, so counting "1 e & a" gives every clap a word, and a rest is a word you say without clapping.

cells.text:
Press Start in the game below. After a bar of count-in, four notes move to the line on every beat: count "1 e & a, 2 e & a" aloud, and press Space or tap the lane as each note reaches it.
Practice until the four hits are even and the next number lands on the beat.

Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. Keep saying the whole count, and clap only on "e & a": the click sounds where your clap is missing.
If the claps drift, clap every word again for a bar.

Press Play below to start the metronome. Clap on each number, on "e" and on "a", and say "&" without a clap.
Practice until the silent "&" takes as long as a clap.

Press Play below to start the drums. Clap a bar of sixteenths, then a bar with a rest on every number, and keep swapping.
Then press Click below to switch the metronome on, and check that the numbers of your count land on it.
{{?bpm}}At a faster tempo the rests get shorter, and each one still takes the time of one word of the count.
